requirement: Describe ENRICH as a pilot Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation randomized parallel study comparing FCU-Heart with standard Family Check-Up in pregnant or recently postpartum mothers and their infants, with the principal effectiveness assessment at 6 months.
acceptable_values: pregnant or postpartum mothers and infants

evidence.text: The protocol describes randomization to FCU-Heart or FCU alone, maternal and child cardiovascular assessments, and 6-month effectiveness and implementation measures.
The analysis plan labels the study a pilot and targets 6-month between-arm cardiovascular-health contrasts.

requirement: Define the control as the standard Family Check-Up ecological assessment, initial interview, questionnaires and parent-child interaction tasks followed by feedback and optional sessions; define FCU-Heart as that same program plus maternal cardiovascular assessment and tailored healthy-eating, weight, stress, smoking, blood-pressure and weight-monitoring content.

evidence.text: The protocol details the standard FCU sequence and the additional cardiovascular feedback and modules in FCU-Heart.

requirement: Define the randomized maternal analysis population and linked child population, including pregnancy or delivery within two months, Medicaid eligibility, Allegheny County residence, English language, exclusion of specified complex chronic conditions and multifetal pregnancies, and rules for eligibility adjudication before randomization.
acceptable_values: pregnant or within two months postpartum

evidence.text: The model-visible protocol identifies pregnant and postpartum women and linked infants but does not fully enumerate the analysis set or eligibility adjudication rules.

requirement: Specify the planned unequal randomization of 100 mothers to FCU-Heart and 50 to FCU alone, state the allocation mechanism and concealment, and reconcile the reference's race-stratified analysis with any randomization strata; do not infer a 1:1 design.

evidence.text: The protocol states that mothers are randomized to two groups but omits allocation implementation details.
The plan uses 100 versus 50 participants and repeats analysis by race stratum without explaining whether race is a design stratum.

requirement: State masking by role and reconcile the registry claim that investigators are masked during delivery and assessment with visibly arm-specific FCU-Heart coaching and device procedures; do not claim participant or coach masking.

evidence.text: The intervention and standard FCU conditions contain visibly different coaching and cardiovascular components, while the protocol does not define masked roles.

requirement: Resolve the primary endpoint hierarchy before analysis: the registry identifies change in postpartum weight retention from post-delivery to 6 months as primary, while the two-page plan treats 6-month blood pressure and weight levels jointly; identify one primary endpoint or an explicit co-primary family.

evidence.text: The protocol names maternal blood pressure, BMI and other cardiovascular measures and a 6-month outcome assessment without a formal primary hierarchy.
The plan jointly focuses on differences in mean 6-month blood pressure and weight.

requirement: Define derivations for postpartum weight retention, 6-month weight, systolic and diastolic blood pressure and BMI, including which prenatal, post-delivery, self-reported or device measurement is baseline, replicate blood-pressure rules and remote-versus-in-person measurement handling.

evidence.text: The protocol names Bluetooth BP, weight and BMI measures and remote control-arm assessment but does not provide endpoint derivation rules.

requirement: Estimate each selected 6-month continuous endpoint by arm using observed sample means, report the FCU-Heart-minus-FCU-alone mean difference, and construct a two-sample t-based 95% confidence interval.

evidence.text: The reference specifies arm sample means, their difference and a two-sample t-based 95% confidence interval.

requirement: Repeat the selected 6-month mean-difference analyses within prespecified race strata, define the race categories and sparse-cell rule, and label these analyses exploratory unless powered interaction testing is separately justified.

evidence.text: The plan says the analysis will be repeated for each race stratum but gives no categories or sparse-data procedure.

requirement: Define the pilot effectiveness estimand for each primary endpoint using all randomized mothers analyzed as assigned, the assigned FCU-Heart versus FCU-alone conditions and the 6-month contrast, with strategies for pregnancy or infant loss, optional-session nonparticipation, intervention discontinuation, outside care and unavailable device measurements.

evidence.text: The protocol includes optional sessions, outside referrals, remote measurements and withdrawal after pregnancy or infant loss.
The plan requires intention-to-treat analysis as randomized but does not define intercurrent-event handling.

requirement: Predefine handling of missing 6-month BP, weight, BMI, questionnaire and Fitbit data, report availability and reasons by arm, and include a sensitivity analysis compatible with the intention-to-treat estimand instead of silently using observed completers.

evidence.text: The protocol uses cloud devices, remote assessments and optional sessions but provides no missing-data analysis.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 150 randomized mothers, 100 FCU-Heart and 50 FCU alone, with approximately 90% retention; report the plan's 13.7% margin-of-error and 82% power statements as design context and do not substitute the registry's later actual enrollment of 117.

evidence.text: The prospective plan gives the unequal target, retention, margin-of-error and power assumptions.

requirement: Use two-sided 95% confidence intervals and interpret the pilot primarily through estimation; if hypothesis tests are reported, define two-sided alpha 0.05 and do not turn the design power statement into an unplanned binary success rule.

evidence.text: The plan emphasizes estimation with 95% confidence while also mentioning 5% significance in the power calculation.

requirement: Define the hierarchy and multiplicity strategy across weight, systolic and diastolic pressure, BMI, diet, activity, smoking, maternal and child measures and race-stratified analyses; otherwise label nonprimary analyses exploratory and avoid familywise confirmatory claims.

evidence.text: The protocol names many maternal, child and implementation measures without an inferential hierarchy.
The reference jointly analyzes BP and weight and repeats by race without multiplicity control.

requirement: Prespecify secondary analyses for maternal diet quality, self-reported and Fitbit physical activity, smoking and child blood pressure/BMI, including scale scoring, device wear or validity rules, timepoint, arm contrast and uncertainty.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies maternal diet, activity, smoking and child cardiovascular measures but no endpoint-specific analysis.

requirement: Define implementation outcomes and denominators for reach, feasibility, acceptability, maintenance, equity, implementation, tailorability, session completion, engagement, Working Alliance and digital literacy, and separate descriptive process evaluation from causal effectiveness claims.

evidence.text: The protocol lists modified FRAME-IT measures, surveys, enrollment, session completion and digital literacy but supplies no quantitative analysis details.

requirement: Prespecify qualitative analysis of FCU-Heart coach interviews, including sampling, coding framework, coder roles, theme development, completeness or saturation and integration with quantitative implementation findings.

evidence.text: The protocol proposes qualitative coach interviews about feasibility, appropriateness and barriers/facilitators without an analysis method.

requirement: Account for recruitment setting and intervention coach where relevant, and evaluate whether remote versus in-person 6-month measurement differs by arm or participant characteristics; do not assume measurement mode is ignorable without assessment.

evidence.text: The program is coach-delivered and the control group's 6-month cardiovascular measurements are remote when possible.

requirement: Define whether adverse events and clinically high BP or weight-related findings are safety outcomes, identify an exposed safety population, and summarize referrals, serious events, severity, relationship and withdrawals including pregnancy or infant loss; otherwise justify why formal safety analysis is not applicable.

evidence.text: The protocol provides referrals for elevated readings and pregnancy or infant loss but no safety analysis plan.

requirement: Keep the two-page Data Analysis Plan annotation-only: the model-visible four-page protocol may expose the two arms, measures and 6-month assessment, but must not expose the reference-only unequal target, t-based interval, race-stratum repetition, power assumptions or analyzed-as-randomized rule.

evidence.text: Full visual review found design and measures but not the reference's executable inferential decisions.
The independent plan contains the t interval, unequal sample, race-stratum, power and intention-to-treat decisions.
